findings.sequence_description: Replay the same SAML Assertion ID that includes <OneTimeUse/> twice under a hardened SAML IdP config; second submission must be rejected.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_otur_victim_login_status < 400 AND user_otur_attacker_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_otur_victim_login_status=200 < 400 → True) AND (user_otur_attacker_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: SAML OneTimeUse assertion was accepted more than once (replay not rejected).

findings.sequence_description: Confirm baseline SAML login works, then harden IdP config and attempt replay of the same Assertion/@ID; second submission must be rejected (replay detection should not be bypassed by config changes).
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_aid_control_login_status < 400 AND user_aid_replay_after_harden_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_aid_control_login_status=200 < 400 → True) AND (user_aid_replay_after_harden_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: SAML Assertion/@ID replay was accepted (or replay cache was bypassed) after IdP configuration change.

findings.sequence_description: Replay a OneTimeUse assertion twice under default config, then harden signature/issuer enforcement and replay again to see if replay protection is still missing or inconsistently applied.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_ot_a_first_login_status == 200 AND user_ot_b_replay_default_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_ot_a_first_login_status=200 == 200 → True) AND (user_ot_b_replay_default_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: SAML OneTimeUse assertion was accepted on replay under default config (OneTimeUse not enforced).

findings.sequence_description: Replay a OneTimeUse assertion twice under default config, then harden signature/issuer enforcement and replay again to see if replay protection is still missing or inconsistently applied.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_ot_c_first_hardened_login_status == 200 AND user_ot_d_replay_hardened_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_ot_c_first_hardened_login_status=200 == 200 → True) AND (user_ot_d_replay_hardened_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: SAML OneTimeUse assertion was accepted on replay after hardening (replay cache missing or bypassed).

findings.sequence_description: Control valid SAML login, then attempt expired assertion acceptance, then replay the same expired assertion ID to test both time-bound enforcement and replay handling on stale artifacts.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_time_attack_expired_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_time_attack_expired_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Expired SAML assertion was accepted (NotOnOrAfter not enforced).

findings.sequence_description: Control valid SAML login, then attempt expired assertion acceptance, then replay the same expired assertion ID to test both time-bound enforcement and replay handling on stale artifacts.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_time_attack_expired_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_time_attack_expired_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Replayed expired SAML assertion (same Assertion/@ID) was accepted; stale artifact reuse not prevented.

findings.sequence_description: I2 attack: replay a OneTimeUse assertion after relaxing signature enforcement mid-test to see if replay cache is incorrectly keyed to verification policy/config.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_first_login_status == 200 AND user_attacker_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_attacker_first_login_status=200 == 200 → True) AND (user_attacker_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: OneTimeUse assertion was accepted more than once (replay succeeded), possibly due to replay cache being keyed to verification policy/config rather than assertion ID.

findings.sequence_description: I2 attack: replay the same Assertion/@ID while changing upstream principal fields (target_identity/email) to see if replay detection is incorrectly scoped to principal rather than assertion ID.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_victim_like_first_login_status == 200 AND user_attacker_like_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_victim_like_first_login_status=200 == 200 → True) AND (user_attacker_like_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: SP accepted the same SAML Assertion/@ID twice when the asserted principal changed, indicating replay detection may be scoped to principal/email rather than assertion ID.

findings.sequence_description: I2 attack: confirm valid login works, then attempt an expired assertion with a fixed ID, then reuse the same fixed ID with a fresh (non-expired) assertion to test whether replay cache is bypassed/poisoned by an expired attempt.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_control_valid_login_status == 200 AND user_attacker_expired_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_control_valid_login_status=200 == 200 → True) AND (user_attacker_expired_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: SP accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past), violating freshness requirements.

findings.sequence_description: I2 attack: confirm valid login works, then attempt an expired assertion with a fixed ID, then reuse the same fixed ID with a fresh (non-expired) assertion to test whether replay cache is bypassed/poisoned by an expired attempt.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_expired_login_status >= 400 AND user_attacker_reuse_fresh_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_attacker_expired_login_status=200 >= 400 → False) AND (user_attacker_reuse_fresh_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: SP accepted reuse of the same Assertion/@ID after an expired attempt, indicating replay cache bypass/poisoning or missing assertion ID tracking.

findings.sequence_description: I2 attack: replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID after revoking the first session to test whether replay protection is incorrectly tied to active sessions rather than assertion ID uniqueness.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Replay accepted: the same SAML Assertion/@ID was accepted again after revoking the first session, indicating replay protection is missing or incorrectly scoped to active sessions.

findings.sequence_description: I3 attack: After a successful SAML broker login under permissive settings, harden signature requirements and ensure the next SAML login is rejected (no stale/old verification policy acceptance).
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: permissive_login_status == 200 AND hardened_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (permissive_login_status=200 == 200 → True) AND (hardened_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: After enabling validateSignature+wantAssertionsSigned, broker still accepted attacker-signed SAML login (stale verification policy / flow coherence failure).

findings.sequence_description: I3 attack: Configure SAML IdP with a Post Login Flow intended to enforce MFA, then attempt broker login and check whether the flow is coherently applied (no step skipping).
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_victim_saml_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_victim_saml_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SAML broker login succeeded even though a Post Login Flow intended to enforce additional steps was configured; indicates potential flow step skipping / non-atomic flow enforcement.

findings.sequence_description: I3 attack: Change SAML principal extraction (principalType/principalAttribute) mid-test and attempt re-auth; ensure no stale session/config splicing allows login under the wrong binding rule.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_bob_saml_after_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_bob_saml_after_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: After changing principal extraction to ATTRIBUTE(email), a SAML login with mismatched target_identity but colliding email was accepted, suggesting stale/previous binding rules or non-atomic flow evaluation across config change.

findings.sequence_description: I3 attack: Change First Login Flow mid-test (linking behavior) and attempt re-auth with same upstream identity; ensure the new flow is applied and no stale sub-session allows bypass of the updated first-login FSM.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_upstream2_after_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_upstream2_after_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: After changing the First Login Flow, a broker login that should have been forced through the updated first-login FSM was accepted, suggesting stale flow state or step skipping across the config change.

findings.sequence_description: I3 flow-coherence under mid-flight realm/client reconfiguration: accept a SAML login, then tighten the SAML client assertion lifespan and immediately attempt a second SAML login using the same Assertion/@ID. The second attempt must be rejected (no stale auth sub-session or config-splicing that allows a replayed assertion to be accepted after policy change).
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_victim_saml_replay_after_tighten_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_victim_saml_replay_after_tighten_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted a replayed SAML Assertion/@ID after a tightening config change, indicating stale/non-atomic flow state or config-splicing across authentication steps.

findings.sequence_description: I5 attack: demonstrate authorization context drift after config change—first enforce trusted Issuer, then relax issuer validation and re-auth with an untrusted Issuer; broker should not grant an authenticated session under relaxed policy if it violates intended broker policy.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_issuer_relaxed_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_issuer_relaxed_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: After relaxing issuer validation, broker accepted an untrusted Issuer assertion, enabling effective permissions outside the intended UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy boundary.

findings.sequence_description: Harden SAML IdP (signature+issuer validation), perform control login, then re-auth with a forged assertion carrying a wrong AudienceRestriction to test audience binding under hardened config.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_aud_control_login_status < 400 AND user_aud_attack_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_aud_control_login_status=200 < 400 → True) AND (user_aud_attack_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: Broker accepted a SAML assertion without Conditions (no audience/time bounds) under hardened signature+issuer configuration, indicating missing authorization binding to upstream intent.

findings.sequence_description: Use a SAML assertion with no <Conditions> and then replay the same Assertion/@ID to see if the broker grants repeated sessions/permissions without temporal/audience constraints (authorization binding to upstream intent is missing).
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_nocond_first_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_nocond_first_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted a SAML assertion without a <Conditions> element, allowing permissions without upstream audience/time constraints.

findings.sequence_description: Use a SAML assertion with no <Conditions> and then replay the same Assertion/@ID to see if the broker grants repeated sessions/permissions without temporal/audience constraints (authorization binding to upstream intent is missing).
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_nocond_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_nocond_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted replay of the same Assertion/@ID for a no-Conditions assertion, enabling repeated authorization without upstream constraints.

findings.sequence_description: I5 attack: Under default SAML IdP broker config (no signature/issuer enforcement), attempt attacker-signed SAML login as a high-privilege identity and then request a broker token for a protected audience. If accepted, effective permissions exceed upstream intent because the broker accepted an unauthenticated proof.
findings.description:
Assertion FAILED: attacker_admin_saml_default_status >= 400

Implication: Broker accepted attacker-signed SAML assertion under default (non-validating) configuration, enabling an authenticated session not bounded by upstream intent.
